plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-db-connections

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**Named database connections** for DeepSeek Harness. Configure your databases in a settings page, then refer to them by name in chat — say "use 128" and the model knows which database to reach and how.

## The problem it solves

Asking an AI to query a database normally means restating host, port, user, and password every time. This plugin stores those in configuration and leaves one short name (`128`) for you and the model to use:

- The connection names are contributed to the system prompt, so "use 128" resolves without you repeating an address or a credential.
- All three tools take `connection` as their first argument, so the model only carries names.
- **No password ever reaches the prompt** — only host, port, default schema, and whether the connection is writable.

## Install

Plugin directory: `<path-to>/dsh-db-connections`

Install dependencies first (`mysql2` and `yaml`):

```sh
cd <path-to>/dsh-db-connections
npm install
```

Then install into a profile with the DSH plugin command. The Electron desktop app owns its `desktop` profile exclusively, so use the CLI the app ships:

```sh
# Default Windows desktop path; substitute your own if installed elsewhere.
"C:\Program Files\deepseek\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd" ^
  plugin --profile desktop add "<path-to>/dsh-db-connections"
```

`dsh plugin add` records the package in the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, and the package's own `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `id: db-connections` row with `connections: []` (connect to nothing by default).

Any other profile (`web`, `tui`, your own) uses the ordinary CLI:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /absolute/path/to/dsh-db-connections
```

> **Restart the desktop app once after installing**, so the settings page appears: the client-plugin roster is scanned at startup, not re-scanned while running.
>
> Conversely, **the plugin directory must not be deleted, renamed, or moved**: the profile references it through a `link:`, and a missing directory produces `cannot resolve profile bundle "dsh-db-connections"`.

## Configure a database

Two routes, one configuration — use whichever you prefer.

### Route 1: click through the app (recommended)

Open **Settings → Databases** to add, edit, and delete connections, pick **read-only** or **read-write** per connection from a dropdown, and press **Test** to verify a connection on the spot. Saving applies immediately — no restart, and no need to touch the configuration file.

The page follows the shell's own language setting (Chinese/English): dictionaries are contributed with `ctx.locale.register()` and lookups go through `ctx.locale.bind()`, rather than guessing from the browser, so the page follows a language switch.

Passwords are shown and edited as plain text: the value lives in a file you own, and hiding it only makes a wrong password impossible to spot.

### Route 2: edit the configuration file

**Redefine** the `db-connections` row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. The loader replaces a row's whole `config` rather than deep-merging it, so restate every key:

```yaml
- id: db-connections
  name: "dsh-db-connections"
  config:
    connections:
      - name: "128"              # the name you and the model use in chat
        host: 192.0.2.10
        port: 3306               # optional, default 3306
        user: root
        password: "change-me"       # or use passwordEnv, below
        database: appdb     # optional default schema
        description: dev database # optional; shown in the prompt
        allowWrite: false        # optional, default false = read-only
```

Where the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` lives:

| Platform | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `C:\Users\<you>\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml` |
| macOS / Linux | `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml` |

Press **Reload** on the settings page, or restart the app, to apply a hand edit. A change made through the settings page needs neither.

### Several connections

`connections` is a list, in order; names must be unique:

```yaml
- id: db-connections
  name: "dsh-db-connections"
  config:
    connections:
      - name: "128"
        host: 192.0.2.10
        user: root
        password: "change-me"
        database: appdb
        description: dev database
      - name: "prod"
        host: 192.0.2.9
        user: readonly_user
        passwordEnv: PROD_DB_PASSWORD   # keeps the secret out of the file
        database: app_prod
        description: production (read-only account)
      - name: "local"
        host: 127.0.0.1
        user: root
        password: ""
        description: local MySQL
```

### Keep the password out of the file

Name an environment variable with `passwordEnv`; it is resolved at load, and a missing variable fails loudly rather than becoming an empty password:

```yaml
        passwordEnv: PROD_DB_PASSWORD
```

When both are present, `passwordEnv` wins. **A settings-page save does not destroy this**: the page edits raw configuration, so a resolved password is never written back to the file. Note the other direction: the settings page has no `passwordEnv` field of its own — creating the indirection is a hand edit of the configuration file.

### Write access

**Set per connection, read-only by default.** The settings page's dropdown ("Read-only" / "Read-write") is exactly the `allowWrite` flag in the configuration file.

Read-only has two independent layers, neither of which is keyword matching in the plugin:

1. With `allowWrite: false` (the default), `db_execute` refuses outright.
2. Even on a writable connection, every `db_query` statement runs inside a server-enforced `START TRANSACTION READ ONLY` — **MySQL rejects the write** — so bypass-shaped statements such as `SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE`, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, and `WITH ... UPDATE` are refused by the server too.

Before enabling writes, confirm the database should accept changes from the agent. A read-only account is the better choice for most deployments than turning on `allowWrite`.

## The three tools

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `db_query` | Read-only queries, in a server-enforced read-only transaction. Returns columns plus rows. |
| `db_execute` | Writes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL). Available only with `allowWrite: true`. |
| `db_schema` | Inspect structure: omit `database` to list schemas; pass `database` to list tables; add `table` for columns, indexes, and DDL. |

You do not call these yourself. Typical requests:

- "list the schemas on 128" → `db_schema`
- "what does sys_user look like in 128?" → `db_schema`
- "show me the first 10 users in 128" → `db_query`
- "change the remark on id=1 in 128" → `db_execute` (needs a writable connection)

## Per-connection options

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | Connection name, unique, ≤64 characters |
| `host` | required | Hostname or IP |
| `user` | required | Account name |
| `password` | `''` | Password, stored as plain text in the configuration file |
| `passwordEnv` | — | Environment variable holding the password; wins over `password` |
| `port` | `3306` | TCP port |
| `driver` | `mysql` | Only `mysql` is supported |
| `database` | — | Default schema; without it, qualify SQL as `schema.table` |
| `description` | — | Shown in the prompt, for context |
| `allowWrite` | `false` | Whether this connection accepts writes; the settings page's read-only / read-write dropdown |
| `ssl` | `false` | Connect over TLS |
| `connectTimeoutMs` | `10000` | Connection timeout |
| `queryTimeoutMs` | `30000` | Per-statement timeout (client and server `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME`) |
| `maxRows` | `200` | Rows returned per call; an excess is reported, never silently dropped |
| `maxCellChars` | `500` | Characters kept per cell |
| `maxDdlChars` | `20000` | Bound for the table DDL `db_schema` returns, kept separate so a CREATE TABLE is not cut off |
| `connectionLimit` | `4` | Pool size |

A bad configuration fails **at plugin load** naming the offending key, rather than when the model first calls a tool.

## Security notes

- Passwords never appear in the prompt or in tool results.
- Read-only comes from a server

plugins.description: A daily Token-usage heatmap for the DSH settings page, including an estimated daily cost in CNY from DeepSeek list prices. Aggregated entirely from local session logs; no external requests. ｜ DSH 设置中的每日 Token 用量热力图，含人民币估算消费金额；数据取自本机会话日志，不发起外部请求。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-token-heatmap

[中文](README.zh.md) | English

A **daily token-usage heatmap** that adds a "Token usage" section to the DSH settings page. One cell per day; theme-aware greyscale indicates relative usage.

Selecting a day also shows an **estimated cost in CNY**, derived from DeepSeek's published list prices and their peak/off-peak schedule.

All data is derived from DSH's own local session logs. **No external network requests and no separate usage ledger.**

> **Privacy**: this plugin makes no outbound requests. Session logs are read on the local machine only, and the aggregated result is served to your local DSH page. The repository contains no personal data or credentials.

## Design highlights

- **A native settings section, not an overlay.** The component registers into the `settings.section` slot and renders React elements only. It does not append to `document.body`, does not replace the application root, and imports no Harness client package. It therefore occupies the settings sidebar alongside the built-in sections rather than floating above the application. See [Implementation notes](#implementation-notes).
- **Local data only, single source of truth.** No data leaves the machine and no additional ledger is required: every figure is derived from the session logs DSH already writes.
- **The session log format is parsed explicitly.** Concatenated zstd frames, replayed `seq` values and truncated tail frames are each handled as distinct cases. A single-pass decompression retains only the first frame of a multi-frame log and therefore under-reports usage. See [Data source](#data-source).
- **Colour levels remain readable at both ends of the scale.** The four metrics differ by orders of magnitude, so levels are derived from **quantiles of the local data set** (25th/50th/75th percentiles) rather than fixed thresholds. Cache reads frequently account for the majority of a day — 99% in the screenshots below — which is why `Input+output` is provided as a separate metric.
- **Brightness is reserved for days with recorded usage.** Days without usage occupy the lowest visual level, so an otherwise empty grid remains visually neutral and days with usage are distinguishable at a glance. This carries an accessibility benefit as well: the encoding never relies on colour hue.
- **Cost is estimated rather than billed.** DSH session logs record token counts but no currency amounts, so the detail panel applies DeepSeek's published CNY prices to the day's input, cache-read and output tokens. The peak/off-peak schedule is accounted for per record using the record's own timestamp, and the panel states that the figure is an estimate. See [Cost estimate](#cost-estimate).
- **Selection and expansion are separate states.** Collapsing a day's details retains its selection outline on the heatmap; selecting another day switches the details directly; `Esc` collapses first and clears the selection second. Reading a sequence of days therefore requires no intermediate close step.
- **Host integration for theme and language.** Colours are drawn from host theme tokens (`--dsw-alias-*`), and all visible text is registered through `ctx.locale.register`, so an application language change re-renders the section. Number units are localized as well (`万`/`亿` in Chinese, `K`/`M`/`B` in English).
- **Regression tests rather than claims.** Five self-test entry points cover frame parsing, deduplication, caching, weekly boundaries, client rendering and route registration. See [Layout](#layout).

## Screenshots

> **Note on screenshot currency.** The images below predate **v0.5.0** and have not been re-captured since. Three UI changes made since are therefore not visible in them:
>
> 1. **Empty-day cells render darker.** Days without recorded usage now occupy the dimmest level, reserving the brightness range for days with usage (v0.4.1).
> 2. **Collapsing a day retains its selection.** Selecting the same date again collapses only the detail body; the selection outline remains on the heatmap and the collapsed row carries an expand control (v0.4.1).
> 3. **The detail panel shows an estimated cost.** A daily cost in CNY is displayed next to the daily total (v0.5.0).
>
> The textual descriptions throughout this document reflect the current behaviour.

### Half-year heatmap and compact tooltip

Open Settings → **Token usage**. The default range is six months. Choose total, input+output, cache read or output, and switch between daily and weekly views. The range selector offers six months or a full year; the year is split into two rows.

Hover a date cell to display three lines: the date (YYYY-MM-DD), the selected metric's Token count, and “Click to view details”. The example below shows 2026-10-13 with a total of 117,405,946 Token. Selecting the cell displays that day's breakdown below the heatmap. The outline indicates hover or selection; today's cell has no default highlight. Cells with no recorded usage remain at the dimmest level, so the brightness range is reserved for days with usage.

![English half-year heatmap and tooltip](docs/heatmap-en.png)

### Inline daily details and Token composition

Selecting a date displays its details inline below the heatmap, without navigating away from the page. A single-line hint above the footnote indicates the interaction until a date is selected. Selecting the same date again collapses the detail body while retaining the selection outline on the heatmap, so the selected date remains identifiable; the collapsed row provides an expand control. Selecting a different date switches the details directly, with no intermediate collapse step. For keyboard users, `Esc` on a focused cell collapses the details, and a second press clears the selection. All filters remain available throughout.

Details include the total, input, output, cache reads and calls, plus cache writes when present, and an estimated daily cost in CNY. The grayscale bar shows each component's share by Token count. The October 13, 2026 example shows 117,405,946 Token, with cache reads accounting for 99.09%. These are screenshot examples; your statistics come from your local logs.

![English daily details and Token composition](docs/detail-en.png)

### Chinese interface

Labels, months, dates and number units follow the host language. The same daily total appears as “1.17 亿” in Chinese and “117.41M” in English.

![Chinese half-year heatmap and tooltip](docs/heatmap-zh.png)

![Chinese daily details and Token composition](docs/detail-zh.png)

## Features

- Default half-year range (26 weeks); full year uses two rows (27 + 26 weeks), each with month labels
- Cells capped at 20px with 4px gaps, sized to the container to avoid horizontal scrollbars
- **Daily / Weekly** views: daily levels or one shared level per natural week; Sunday–Saturday, future dates empty
- **Four metrics**: total / input+output / cache read / output, rendered in theme-aware grayscale
- Hover or focus shows the cell's date, the selected metric's Token count and a click hint; weekly counts are labeled
- Click a date for inline daily details below the heatmap: total, input, output, cache reads, calls, nonzero cache writes, and an estimated cost in CNY; weekly cells open their actual day
- Selecting the selected date again collapses the detail body while retaining its selection outline; an expand control and `Esc` both collapse, and selecting another date switches without an intermediate collapse
- **Cost estimate** based on DeepSeek's published CNY prices, including the peak/off-peak schedule applied per record timestamp; unknown models fall back to the Flash table and are labelled as such. The English interface writes `CNY ¥4.98` so the currency is explicit.
- Proportional Token composition bar with percentages and an empty state
- Approximately 600ms diagonal entrance without delaying the summary; filters and date selection do not replay it
- Native buttons support Enter/Space and focus feedback; respects system reduced-motion preferences
- Today / this week / all-time summary; minute refresh plus refresh on visibility or focus
- Chinese/English labels, month names and number units; follows the host light/dark th

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: treat a real Android phone as a device the agent can inspect and tidy up over adb — free up storage, find what is eating the disk, clear caches, uninstall, screenshot. No root required. / 免 root 的手机设备管家：查存储、清缓存、卸载应用、截图。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-phone-butler

**把一台真实的 Android 手机，变成 agent 可以查看和打理的一台设备 —— 全部走 adb，不需要 root。**

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that puts a real
Android phone within reach of the agent: free up storage, find what is eating the disk, measure
directories, clear an app cache without touching its data, uninstall, screenshot.

```
phone_status   is a phone reachable, and what is it
phone_scan     read-only: cleanup survey · per-app data sizes · caches · usage · big files
phone_fs       ls / du on /sdcard
phone_act      the only writer: clear-cache · rm · uninstall   (each gated by confirm=true)
phone_shot     screenshot to a local file
```

Plus one bundled skill, `phone-butler`: the capability map, the connection recipes and the five
traps that produced wrong answers.

---

## 为什么值得存在

「手机空间满了」这件事，通常被三个互相矛盾的印象搅在一起：文件管理器说能清，系统设置说
腾不出空间，而真正的元凶躺在一个看不见的目录里。

这个插件做两件具体的事：

1. **把可清理的与不可清理的分开说。** `/sdcard` 全层（**含每个 App 的 `Android/data` 与
   `Android/obb`**）可读写；`/data/data` 未 root 一律碰不到 —— 那是聊天数据库住的地方。
   把这两层混为一谈，是大多数"手机管家"话术的来源。
2. **让那层碰不到的东西至少可以被度量。** `phone_scan kind=apps` 解析
   `dumpsys diskstats` 的并列数组，**未 root 也能列出每个 App 的私有数据大小**（它同时覆盖
   `/data/data` 与外部 `Android/data`）。所以"到底是哪个 App 吃掉了手机"有了确定答案，
   而不是靠猜。

## 安装

在 DSH 里，用官方的 bundle 安装姿势指向本目录（或它的克隆）：

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle  target: <本目录绝对路径>
```

它需要 `adb`：在 `PATH` 里，或用 `DSH_PHONE_ADB` 指向具体可执行文件，或放在 Android SDK
的常规位置。可选配置（在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里覆盖）：

```yaml
- id: dsh-phone-butler
  config:
    adbPath: 'C:\platform-tools\adb.exe'
    timeoutMs: 240000
```

## 安全立场（这是设计里最要紧的部分）

- **读永远不改动任何东西。**
- **写必须显式 `confirm: true`**；否则工具**什么都不执行**，只返回它本来会执行的计划 ——
  把计划摆给用户看、得到同意，再发一次。
- **`rm` 只接受 `/sdcard` 之下的路径**，其它一律拒绝（含测试断言）。
- **扫描默认不列文件名。** 一份来自某人 Download 文件夹的文件清单默认是隐私；`names: true`
  是一次明确的索要。
- **Android 没有回收站。** `rm` 就是最终结果。

## 能力边界（实测，不是推测）

| 层 | 能否触达 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `/sdcard/**` | **可以，读写皆可** | 含每个 App 的 `Android/data`、`Android/obb` |
| `/data/data/<pkg>` | **不可以** | 未 root `Permission denied`；`run-as` 拒绝非 debuggable 包 |
| 每个 App 的数据**大小** | **可以** | `dumpsys diskstats`（覆盖私有层） |
| 只清缓存 | **可以** | `pm clear --cache-only <pkg>`，数据保留 |
| 清空 App 数据 | 技术上可以，但会毁数据 | 本插件**故意不暴露** |

## 连接手机（最容易踩空的一段）

有两条互相独立的通道，行为完全不同：

| 通道 | 绑在哪 | 离开 Wi-Fi 还活着吗 |
|---|---|---|
| **无线调试**（Android 11+） | **WLAN**（开关原文：「连接到 WLAN 后启用调试模式」） | **不活** —— 关掉 Wi-Fi，adbd 就不再监听 |
| **`adb tcpip 5555`** | adbd 进程本身，监听 `0.0.0.0:5555` | **活着** —— 远程能力就靠这个 |

所以想让不在同一网络的手机可达：先在同一个 Wi-Fi 下执行**一次** `adb tcpip 5555`；此后手机
一直听着 5555，任何能路由到它地址的人（例如经过 Tailscale 这类 VPN）都能
`adb connect <手机地址>:5555` 连上。手机重启后失效，需要重做。

找无线调试端口：`adb mdns services` 会直接打印 `IP:端口`。

## 五个会产出错误结论的坑

1. **`find /sdcard` 静默返回空。** `/sdcard` 是符号链接
   （`/sdcard → /storage/self/primary → /storage/emulated/0`），toybox 的 `find` 默认不跟随。
   结果是一份空列表和退出码 0 —— 与"这台手机很干净"完全无法区分。
   **必须 `find -H /sdcard`。** 有一次"没有大文件、没有空目录"的报告就是这么来的，
   而那台手机两样都有几千个。
2. **别把带双引号的命令经 PowerShell 递给 `adb shell`。** 引号会被吃掉，管道错位，
   得到一个静默的空结果。用 argv 数组传参。
3. **推到手机上的脚本必须是 LF 换行。** CRLF 会让 shell 报 `id\r: inaccessible or not found`。
4. **全黑的截图是锁屏，不是抓取失败** —— 比文件大小（约 18 KB 黑屏 vs 几 MB 有内容），
   或查 `dumpsys power`。
5. **别从截图里读路径。** OCR 会混淆 `l`/`1`、`I`/`1`。问设备：`pm path <包名>`。

## 它不是什么（以及为什么不往那边走）

有人会问：既然能看屏幕、能读传感器清单、能注入点击，为什么不把它做成「手机的感知器官」？

我们认真评估过，**结论是不做**。理由放在这里，因为后来的人一定会再问一遍：

| 想法 | 为什么不做 |
|---|---|
| 调相机「以固定采样率看世界」 | `adb shell` 没有 CAMERA 权限，唯一路径是截「相机在前台时的屏幕」—— 那不是采样，是**偷看屏幕**；而且无法验证这一帧真是相机画面，最坏会混进通知栏、私聊弹窗、验证码。 |
| 读传感器数值 | Android 12+ 对 shell 主动遮蔽（`[value masked]`）。能拿到的是**清单**与**事件时间戳**，拿不到读数。 |
| 失联自动求援 | adb 是「桌面端主动连手机」。**唯一需要它的时刻，它必然不在线。** |
| 代做「需要本人承诺」的事 | 见下。 |

**一条判据**（评估过所有候选之后，最好用的那一句）：

> **操作结束后，用户还能不能说「这是我做的、我理解的」？**
> **能就做，不能就别做。**

完整的评估记录 —— 实测边界表、「假成功」七陷阱、L0~L3 分级授权模型、以及两个真正值得做的方向 ——
在 [`docs/design-notes.md`](docs/design-notes.md)。

## 一条共存提醒

如果同一台电脑上有多个 agent，它们**共用同一个 adb server**。`adb kill-server` 会把所有人
一起断掉；只断自己那条，用 `adb disconnect <地址>`。

## 开发

```
node test/selftest.mjs            # 离线断言（纯函数 + 引擎安全语义 + 注册形状）
node test/selftest.mjs --device   # 另跑一轮真实的只读调用
```

`lib/adb.js` 是纯 Node，不从 DSH 导入任何东西 —— 所以引擎可以脱离 harness 直接测试。
`lib/entry.js` 同样零 DSH 导入：一个装在 profile 之外的 `link:` 插件无法解析
`@deepseek-ai/*`，一次这样的 import 就会让整个入口加载失败。

## License

MIT © 2026 Void-LifeStream

---

*实测环境：REDMI K90 Pro Max（第五代骁龙 8 至尊版）/ Xiaomi HyperOS 4.0.2.0（Android 17）/ 无 root 的 adb shell。
下面的每一条限制都是在这台机器上量出来的，不是推断 —— 换机型可能不同，尤其「注入是否被静默忽略」与「传感器数值是否被遮蔽」这两条。*

plugins.description: DSH 1.5 能力组合器：按会话或工作区编排工具、技能与 MCP，按需缩小系统提示。仅支持 DSH 1.5，后续会跟进更新。 / Capability composer for DSH 1.5: per-session tool / skill / MCP compositions that shrink the system prompt on demand. DSH 1.5 only; newer releases will follow.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-capability-composer

**The resident tool surface collapses into a few switchable sets, shrinking the system prompt on demand.**

> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.

> 🟢 **Collision risk: very low.** It occupies **one server-side seam (`system-prompt/assemble`)** — only **4** plugins here share it — and its **two client slots are both `list` / `keyed`** (stackable, one cell per key), never `chain`. See [Compatibility](#compatibility).

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-1.5-4c6ef5.svg)](#compatibility)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#compatibility)

**Shrink what the model sees, not what is running.**

---

## Table of contents

- [What this is](#what-this-is)
- [What it does (four mechanisms)](#what-it-does-four-mechanisms)
- [How a composition is resolved (three levels)](#how-a-composition-is-resolved-three-levels)
- [UI](#ui)
- [Screenshots](#screenshots)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [HTTP API](#http-api)
- [🔗 Integration](#-integration)
- [Known limitations (stated plainly)](#known-limitations-stated-plainly)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [FAQ](#faq)
- [Repository layout](#repository-layout)
- [Self-check](#self-check)
- [License](#license)

---

## What this is

By default DSH stuffs all of the following **into every single request**:

| What gets stuffed in | Measured size |
|---|---|
| **Tool schema** registered by every installed plugin | 414 tool definitions / ~65.6K tokens |
| The **catalog of all skills** | ~76K tokens as a baseline |
| The **system-prompt section** registered by each plugin | `agent-teams:usage` ≈1296 tok + `plugin:dsh-docker` ≈579 tok + `plugin:api-client` ≈254 tok |

Every request pays for "the things you might use", while only a few of them are actually useful in this turn.

`dsh-capability-composer` groups these into **compositions**, and **only lets the current composition into the context**.

### What it does / what it does not do

Let's make the boundary clear first, because this is where misunderstandings happen most easily:

| ✅ It does | ❌ It does not |
|---|---|
| Narrow **the plugin catalog the model sees** | Never turns off any plugin — plugin processes keep running, the UI keeps showing them |
| Shadow **skill catalog entries** that are not on the list | Never removes skills — `/skill-name` can still be invoked manually |
| Make tools **non-resident by default** (keeping only the core + meta tools) | Does not restrict execution — `invoke_tool` can call anything by default |
| Prune the **system-prompt sections** registered by plugins, according to the composition | Does not touch committed history |
| Resolve compositions at the session / workspace / global levels | Does not modify any third-party plugin file on disk |

In one sentence: **it shrinks "the catalog the model can see", not "the things that are running".** Plugins keep running, skills stay available, tools stay callable — all that changes is how much gets stuffed into each request.

---

## What it does (four mechanisms)

### ① Tools are non-resident by default

**Only 31 are resident**: the 28 official core tools, plus 3 meta tools — `search_plugins` / `load_plugin` / `invoke_tool`.

All other tools **never enter the tools list**. The model sees them in the catalog section of the system prompt (section heading `# 可用插件与 MCP 工具`), and calls them directly when needed:

```js
invoke_tool({ tool: "mcp__vnpy__run_backtest", args: { ... } })
```

Use `load_plugin` when a whole group needs to be loaded:

```js
load_plugin({ ids: ["mcp:vnpy"] })
```

**The granularity is "plugin", not "tool name".** This is deliberate: finer granularity was tried — after 417 / 211 tool names were compressed away, the model had no idea what to search for, which made things harder to use instead. The granularity now is the plugin.

Mounting it prints one log line saying so:

```
工具按需加载已挂载：常驻白名单 28 个 + 元工具 3 个（其余全部按需；组合只决定可见范围）
```

### ② Skill shadowing (not disabling)

A skill that is not in the current skill composition gets a **shadow entry with the same name** registered:

- `invocation.modelInvocable: false` — does not enter the skill catalog the model can see and auto-invoke
- `rank: 0` — the lowest rank wins, shadowing the original skill

**`/skill-name` can still be invoked manually.**

One shadow entry is mounted at the global level, and every agent gets one more at the **"nearest level"**, so that session-level compositions also take effect at the agent dimension.

### ③ Plugin compositions narrow "the model's plugin catalog"

Narrowing happens **when the catalog section is generated**, not by unloading plugins.

There are **two lines that are never narrowed**:

- **MCP server lines** — one line per MCP server; the tools inside a server are not governed by compositions
- **The "unassigned tools" fallback line** — tools that cannot be attributed to any plugin are always kept

### ④ System-prompt sections registered by plugins are pruned by composition too

Plugin compositions **cannot control** "the system-prompt sections a plugin registers for itself" — those are inserted by the plugin itself in `system-prompt/assemble`, and are a different thing from the catalog section.

This plugin's `prunePluginSections()` is the only place that can prune them according to the current plugin composition.

Measured saving: **≈2129 tokens / request**:

| Section | Size |
|---|---|
| `agent-teams:usage` | ≈1296 tok |
| `plugin:dsh-docker` | ≈579 tok |
| `plugin:api-client` | ≈254 tok |

**Fail-open design** — better to prune too little than to prune by mistake:

- A section whose owner cannot be identified is always kept
- A section without a namespace is always kept
- When the visible plugin list is empty, **nothing is pruned**, and the log records 「没有『不在组合里』的依据，宁可留着」
- When the plugin list cannot be obtained, nothing is pruned either

Every drop prints one line of evidence to the log.

It can be turned off with `DSH_COMPOSER_PRUNE_PLUGIN_SECTIONS=0`.

---

## How a composition is resolved (three levels)

**The rule is "the nearest level that specifies something wins" — not a strict override.**

| Level | Description |
|---|---|
| 1. **Session** | specified for the current session alone |
| 2. **Workspace** | specified for the current working directory (`cwd`) |
| 3. **Global** | `pinned[axis]['*']` |

A few easy-to-get-wrong points:

- **An empty string / an empty array / `null` all count as "not specified"** and keep inheriting from the level above — they do not mean "specified as empty"
- **A single level can select several entries**; the union is taken
- **An empty list = no filtering** (not "select none"). To select none, use `__none__`

The UI shows which level the current one comes from: 『当前会话』 / 『当前工作区』 / 『全局』 (Session / Workspace / Global).

---

## UI

It installs into DSH's **Settings → Plugins**, adding two tabs:

### Plugin compositions

Decides which plugins appear in **the model's plugin catalog**.

### Skill compositions

Decides which skills appear in **the model's skill catalog**. You can create a composition, rename it, delete it (with a second confirmation), rename a series, delete a series, select all / select none, and search skills.

### Changes take effect immediately, no restart needed

- UI changes are **debounced by 400 ms**, then `POST /dsh-capability-composer/state`
- After the host writes to disk, the state is refreshed immediately

### Saving merges item by item per composition name, not a whole-state overwrite

The server state is the base; only composition names that **actually exist** in the local draft are overwritten. So a composition created elsewhere will not be accidentally deleted by this UI.

The trade-off: a composition deleted here will be "resurrected" if it still exists on the server. **This is a deliberately conservative direction** — losing a composition costs far more than keeping one extra composition.

plugins.description: For DSH to connect to GitHub
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-github

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Connect GitHub repositories to [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): let the agent clone your repositories, read and edit files, commit, and push back to the remote — within the permissions you grant. The first time credentials are needed it asks you to bind a GitHub account, and every later call uses that account by default.

- **Plain ESM JavaScript, no build step, zero runtime dependencies** — it imports no `@deepseek-ai/*` package, so it cannot fail to load because a package did not resolve
- **Account binding** — a first-run prompt collects a PAT once and remembers it; multiple accounts can be bound and switched
- **Read-only-safe by default** — `allowPush` and `allowApiWrite` default to `false`; writing to a remote must be enabled explicitly
- **Credentials never land in the repository, the command line, or the model's context** (see [Security model](#6-security-model))

## 1. Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `gh_account` | `bind` (prompts for a token when none is passed), `list`, `use` (switch the default account), `remove`, `status` |
| `gh_repo` | `clone` (or fetch an existing clone), `status`, `diff`, `log`, `branches`, `create` (create a remote repository) |
| `gh_file` | `get` (line-numbered window), `list`, `put` (whole-file write/create), `edit` (exact replacement — `oldText` must be unique or `count` must be given) |
| `gh_commit` | Stage and commit; `push: true` commits and pushes in one step |
| `gh_push` | Push to `origin` (gated by `allowPush`; `force` uses `--force-with-lease` only and needs `allowForcePush`) |
| `gh_pull` | Pull from the remote (defaults to `--ff-only`, so a divergence fails loudly instead of creating a merge; `rebase: true` switches to rebase) |
| `gh_config` | `status` (credential source and account, **never the token**), `set`, `unset` — operates on a bare token in the DSH credential service |
| `gh_api` | Call the GitHub REST API directly (issues, PRs, Actions, search, …). `GET`/`HEAD` are read-only; writes need `allowApiWrite: true` |

Typical flow:

```
gh_account(action=bind)            # first run: bind an account (or let the first call that needs credentials prompt)
  → gh_repo(action=clone, repo="owner/repo")
  → gh_file(action=get/edit/put)
  → gh_commit(message="…")
  → gh_push()
```

## 2. Install

Node.js ≥ 20 is required (the runtime bundled with DSH is fine).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add github:liufangrui1105/dsh-plugin-github
```

For the desktop profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:liufangrui1105/dsh-plugin-github
```

A local directory or a packed tarball works too:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-plugin-github
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-plugin-github-0.1.0.tgz   # output of pnpm pack
```

Then **fully quit and restart DeepSeek Harness**, and ask it to list the `gh_*` tools it can use.

> This plugin is plain JavaScript: `src/` *is* the runnable artifact, so it needs
> **no `prepare` build script and no `allowBuilds` approval**. The package deliberately defines no
> `prepare` / `build` / `install` script — their mere presence makes npm rebuild the dependency on every install.

> **Upgrading**: a GitHub install resolves the default branch. After changing the code, run
> `add github:liufangrui1105/dsh-plugin-github` again so pnpm re-resolves it, then **restart DSH**.
> Hot reload only reloads modules already loaded; it does not re-fetch dependencies. This is easy to
> mistake for "my change had no effect".

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-plugin-github
```

## 3. Binding a GitHub account

**Option A — let it ask (recommended)**

The first time an operation needs credentials (push, pull, create repository), the plugin opens an input box asking for a Personal Access Token. It validates the token against `/user` first, stores it only on success, and makes it the default account; every later call uses it without asking again.

You can also trigger it explicitly:

```
gh_account(action="bind")                      # open the input box
gh_account(action="bind", token="ghp_xxxx")    # pass the token directly
```

**Option B — without going through the conversation**

If you would rather the token never appear in the session transcript, provide it out of band: set `GITHUB_TOKEN` before starting DSH, or write it into `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`:

```yaml
version: 1
refs:
  GITHUB_TOKEN: ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Resolution order (first hit wins): **bound account → environment variable → `refs:` in `.credentials.yaml` → workspace `.env`**. A bound account always wins, so "I bound X" is never silently overridden by a `GITHUB_TOKEN` that happens to exist in the environment.

Minimum PAT scope: **`repo`** for read/write repository content (for a fine-grained token, Contents: Read and write); Contents: Read is enough for read-only use. Use `gh_account(action="status")` or `gh_config(action="status")` to check the effective account and remaining rate limit.

**Multiple accounts**: each `bind` accumulates, and the most recent binding becomes the default. Switch with `gh_account(action="use", login="…")` and delete with `action="remove"`.

## 4. Configuration

Configuration lives under the plugin row's `config:` in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (that file replaces the whole `config` value; it does not deep-merge).

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `workspaceRoot` | host process working directory | Root for local clones. **Every `gh_*` path is confined to this directory** |
| `gitExecutable` | `git` | The git executable to run. Set it when git lives somewhere unusual — a bundled runtime, a portable install — instead of editing `PATH` |
| `allowRepos` | `[]` | Repository allowlist: `owner/repo`, `owner/*`, `*/repo`, `*`. Empty means no restriction by repository name. **Only strict `owner/repo` is accepted; full URLs are rejected** |
| `allowPush` | `false` | Allow pushing and creating remote repositories. **While off, `gh_push` and `gh_commit{push:true}` are refused outright** |
| `allowForcePush` | `false` | Allow `--force-with-lease` (still requires `allowPush`) |
| `allowApiWrite` | `false` | Allow `POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE` on `gh_api`, and `gh_repo action=create` |
| `allowApiReadOutsideAllowlist` | `false` | Set `true` to let read-only `gh_api` reach repositories outside the allowlist (e.g. searching public repositories) |
| `allowNonGithubRemotes` | `false` | Allow remotes other than `github.com` (self-hosted Git). **Off by default**: the allowlist constrains `owner/repo` but not the host, so allowing any host means allowing the PAT to be sent anywhere |
| `allowAutoBind` | `true` | Whether to prompt for account binding when credentials are needed |
| `promptForToken` | `true` | Whether the prompt may collect a pasted token |
| `accountStorePath` | `$DSH_HOME/github-accounts.json` | Account file path (used only when the DSH credential service is not mounted) |
| `tokenRef` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Credential reference name (the key under `refs:` in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`) |
| `tokenEnv` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Environment variable to fall back to (then `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN`) |
| `dotenv` | `true` | Also fall back to `.env.local` / `.env` in the workspace |
| `commandTimeoutMs` | `120000` | Timeout for a single git command |
| `maxDiffChars` / `maxReadChars` | `20000` / `40000` | Cap on content returned to the model |
| `gitAuthorName` / `gitAuthorEmail` | unset | Commit author; unset means the git global configuration |

Enabling writes:

```yaml
- id: github-repo
  config:
    allowPush: true
    allowApiWrite: true
    allowRepos:
      - your-name/your-repo
    workspaceRoot: '/path/to/clones'
```

## 5. Authorization model

An allowlist and a credential must be judged against **the object actually acted on**, never against a string derived from the arguments. This is the area an independent audit attacked, and every item below is a fix for it:

- **Local directories are named `owner__repo`**, so same-named repositories under different owners cannot collide into one directory.
- **The real remote

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: normalize tool schemas before the model request (fixes Gemini functionDeclarations 400s from any MCP or built-in tool)
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-gemini-tool-schema

> Normalize the tool schemas sent to the model into the **strict OpenAPI 3.0 subset that Gemini's function declarations accept**. A TypeScript plugin for DeepSeek Harness.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-gemini-tool-schema.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-gemini-tool-schema)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-gemini-tool-schema.svg)](LICENSE)
[![ci](https://github.com/ChenXu233/dsh-gemini-tool-schema/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ChenXu233/dsh-gemini-tool-schema/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

## The problem

Strict providers accept only a *subset* of JSON Schema. Google Gemini's `functionDeclarations[].parameters` rejects the **whole request** (HTTP 400) when:

| Real error | Offending schema | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema didn't specify the schema type field` | `{ anyOf: [{type:'string',…}, {type:'null'}] }` — no `type` | Playwright MCP `browser_emulate_media.colorScheme` (`z.string().nullable()`) |
| `properties[v_types].items: missing field` | `{ type: 'array' }` — no `items` | Lingshu MCP `lingshu_cg` / `lingshu_stg` (19 params) |
| `properties[permission].enum[3]: cannot be empty` | `enum: [..., '']` | DSH built-in `task_board_update.permission` |

All three are legal elsewhere, which is why the failure only shows up on a Gemini-flavoured route.

## Why a Harness hook

An MCP proxy only reaches the servers it wraps. Built-in tools and tools registered by other plugins never cross an MCP transport, so normalizing at Harness assembly time is the only fix that covers **every** tool at once.

## Install

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ChenXu233/dsh-gemini-tool-schema.git
cd dsh-gemini-tool-schema && npm install && npm run build
```

Append to `<DSH home>/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: gemini-tool-schema
      name: '/absolute/path/to/dsh-gemini-tool-schema/dist/index.js'
      config:
        mode: list
        apis: ['gemini', 'google', 'vertex']
```

Or `npm install dsh-gemini-tool-schema` and mount it by package name.

## Configuration

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `list` | `all` every request · `list` matching APIs only · `off` disabled |
| `apis` | `['gemini','google','vertex']` | API patterns, **compiled as regular expressions** |
| `unknownApi` | `apply` | When the route cannot be read: `apply` or `skip` |
| `itemsFallback` | `{type:'string'}` | Element schema for arrays that omit `items` |
| `nullable` | `true` | Emit `nullable: true` for null unions |
| `dryRun` | `false` | Report and lint, but send the original schemas |
| `logFile` / `logLevel` | none / `info` | One diagnostic line per assembly |
| `dumpDir` / `dumpSchemas` | none / `true` | Dump the model-facing tool set for offline auditing |

Patterns match against `provider/model` (e.g. `gemini-lumiya/gemini-4-argon`) and accept substring, regex, and `/pattern/flags` forms; an entry that does not compile degrades to a case-insensitive substring match. `'*'` matches everything, or set `mode: all`.

## Rules

Every node gets a `type`; every array gets `items`; `enum` entries are never empty (and `const` cannot reintroduce one); `$ref`/`$defs` are inlined cycle-safely; unsupported keywords are stripped and the remaining scalars pass an allow-list; `required` is narrowed to real properties.

## Development

```sh
npm test        # Node ≥22.6 runs the TS tests directly — 36 tests
npm run build   # tsc → dist/
```

## License

MIT © 2026 ChenXu233

plugins.description: 给 DSH 用的开发日志插件。自动记录"为什么"和"踩了什么坑"。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-devlog

DSH 插件：在每轮工作结束时，自动把这一轮的上下文加工成一段开发日志，追加到本地文件。

开发者每天写完代码就忘了写日志。这个插件替你记——今天干了什么、为什么这么干、踩了什么坑。

## 定位

- 面向开发者本人的开发日志，不是 CHANGELOG，不是会话摘要
- 读者只有开发者自己
- 验证"上下文 + 记忆 + 检查点 → 自动总结"这套机制在 DSH 生态里跑不跑得通

生态位上，dsh-memory 类负责"记"（输出给 Agent 的记忆片段），dsh-git-commit 类负责"提交"，dsh-trail-plugin 类负责"找"。这个插件填的是空缺的那一环：把上下文和记忆里的技术讨论，加工成面向开发者本人的开发日志。

## 闭环

```
agent/turn-stopping → 切片过滤本轮事件 → 模型判断/生成 → 追加落盘
```

1. 监听 `agent/turn-stopping`（serial 钩子，只观察不 steer）
2. 从 `session/event` 订阅缓冲切出本轮事件，过滤噪音（系统消息、plugin/skill-catalog 注入、request/header、session/title 等）
3. 调模型（deepseek-flash）把材料加工成第一人称开发日志；没有实质内容模型输出 SKIP，不写
4. 追加写入 `$DSH_HOME/devlog/YYYY-MM-DD.md`，每段以二级标题开头，不写日期（日期由外层统一加），只追加不重写

## 项目位置

本仓库（clone 后的目录）是独立项目目录，代码、依赖、测试全在这里。

插件本身不在 `$DSH_HOME` 下，DSH 主目录只被读取、不被污染：挂载靠 `--patch <仓库目录>/cordis.patch.yml`。

注意：主 `cordis.patch.yml` 里 `name` 用的是**包名** `dsh-devlog-auto`（不是绝对路径），因此通过 `dsh plugin add dsh-devlog-auto` 或桌面端插件管理器安装后可直接解析，跨机器无需改路径。只有 `tests/` 下的两个探针 patch 仍写绝对路径——它们是本地开发工具，不随 npm 包发布（见 `files` 字段），clone 到别的机器重跑探针时才需要改。

## 目录结构

```
dsh-devlog/  （仓库根目录）
├── index.js          # 插件主逻辑（监听/切片过滤/生成/落盘）
├── cordis.patch.yml  # patch 层，一行 insert（name 为包名 dsh-devlog-auto）
├── package.json      # type: module
├── node_modules/     # 依赖：schemastery 3.18.4（volatile 字段必需）
├── prompts/
│   ├── system.md     # 系统提示词初始默认值（可在设置页改，见下）
│   └── task.md       # 任务提示词模板（{{date}} 等变量）
├── tests/
│   ├── probe1/       # 探测 1：挂 turn-stopping，dump 事件载荷结构
│   └── probe2/       # 探测 2：确认 prepareCall 形态 + source 字段 + volatile 配置
└── README.md
```

## 安装 / 本地挂载

```bash
cd <仓库目录>
npm install          # 装本地依赖（开发用）

# 作为 DSH 插件安装（已发布到 npm）：
npm install dsh-devlog-auto
```

跑 DSH 时挂上（把路径换成你 clone 下来的仓库目录）：

```bash
dsh --profile headless --patch <仓库目录>/cordis.patch.yml "<你的任务>"
```

或把 `cordis.patch.yml` 里的 insert 行合并进 `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` 常驻。

## 依赖说明：为什么 schemastery 是硬依赖

`@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 被**固定锁死为 `3.18.4` 的 `dependencies`**，而没有按生态惯例放进 `peerDependencies`，原因是：

设置页可编辑的 `logPrompt` 依赖 schemastery 的 `.volatile()`（3.18.4 才提供），而 DSH 宿主内置的是 3.18.2，没有 volatile。若改成 peer 依赖并回落到宿主版本，`logPrompt` 会退化成普通字符串——默认值仍在（日志照样生成），但**设置页编辑能力会丢失**。

所以这里刻意保留硬依赖。代价是与"由宿主统一提供 schemastery"的生态惯例不一致，安装时 pnpm 可能打出 peer warnings，属预期行为，不影响运行。

重跑探测脚本（改插件 API 用法前值得先跑一遍确认形态）：

```bash
dsh --profile headless --patch <仓库目录>/tests/probe2/cordis.yml "回复：probe-ok"
```

## 输出目录

默认是 `$DSH_HOME/devlog/`（即 `~/.dsh/devlog`，DSH 默认家目录），符合"插件把产物写进 DSH 主目录"的语义。

想让产物也离开 DSH 主目录，就在设置页填 `outputDir`（例如 `$DSH_HOME/devlog` 或任意你指定的绝对路径）——留空则用默认。运行时日志和 debug dump 会跟着一起走。

## 设置页可配置项

系统提示词不写死在文件里，模型与调试选项也都走 Config（均可在设置页改）：

```js
Config: {
  logPrompt: z.string().default(<prompts/system.md 内容>).volatile(),  // 系统提示词（volatile，可热改）
  blocking: z.boolean().default(true),                  // 阻塞开关
  provider: z.string().default('deepseek-official'),    // 生成模型 provider
  model: z.string().default('deepseek-flash'),          // 生成模型名
  reasoningEffort: z.string().default('low'),           // 思维链强度（low/high；flash 无 none）
  debugDump: z.string().default('on-error'),            // 调试材料落盘：always / on-error / off
  outputDir: z.string().default(''),                    // 日志目录；留空 = $DSH_HOME/devlog
}
```

- `logPrompt`：在 DSH 设置页的插件卡片里编辑，保存后生效；生成时用 `config.logPrompt.get()` 读当前值。已知限制：host（cordis 4.0.2）不识别 volatile，改配置保存后会重启插件（新值生效，非无感热替换）。`prompts/system.md` 是这个字段的**初始默认值**。
- `provider` / `model` / `reasoningEffort`：生成用的模型与思维链强度。默认 deepseek-flash + low，日志加工足够；换模型/档位按需改。
- `debugDump`：调试材料（喂给模型的完整上下文 + 原始事件）落盘策略。
  - `always`：每轮都写 `.devlog-context-debug.txt`（含你的代码/工具回显，**默认不开启**）
  - `on-error`：仅生成失败/异常时写，便于排查（默认）
  - `off`：从不写
  - 文件落在日志目录下，不在意可定期删。

## blocking 开关

- `blocking: true`（默认）：轮次关闭前等日志写完，headless 模式下产物必然落盘
- `blocking: false`：立即放行轮次，生成在后台跑。交互模式延迟低，但进程退出可能丢未完成的生成

## 运行时日志与调试产物

都在 `$DSH_HOME/devlog/` 下：

- `.devlog-runtime.log` —— 每次跳过/生成/落盘/报错，含材料长度、裁剪档位、生成耗时，排查首选
- `.devlog-context-debug.txt` —— 每次喂给模型的**完整材料** + 原始事件结构 dump（每轮覆盖）

第二个文件的价值：**看不到材料就是盲飞**。第一版曾经因为字段名解析错位，让模型只拿到一条用户指令在凭空写日志（材料 133 字符），产物全是编的——靠这个 dump 才抓出来。调提示词时也值得对着它看。

注意：这个文件里是完整轮次内容（含文件正文、工具回显），不在意的话可以定期清掉。

## 时间基准（踩过的坑）

轮次材料里会带当天更早的日志段（`{{existing_log_today}}` 用于避免重复）。模型容易把这些更早段落误当成"昨天写的"，进而写出"昨天我说过……"这种带偏时间基准的句子。

`prompts/task.md` 顶部专门写了一段时间澄清：已有日志是今天更早写的、早先段落里的"昨天"是相对今天而言、引用时段必须基于材料里真实对应的时间段。别删这一段。

## 第一版不做

- 时间戳分段触发
- 手动全量收口覆盖
- PPT 输出
- 扣子 Skill 那条线

plugins.description: Strata model server monitor panel for DeepSeek Harness: monitor page, floating window, composer status line.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-strata-monitor

在 DeepSeek Harness 里嵌入 Strata 模型服务器的状态监控面板。
A model-server monitor panel for DeepSeek Harness, mirroring the Strata server's Monitor tab.

## 功能 / Features

- **监控页 / Monitor page**：侧边栏新增图标，展示模型状态（空闲 / 读取提示词 / 生成中 / 排队）、解码与预填充速度、GPU 负载、显存、温度、功耗、PCIe、CPU、磁盘读取（均带历史曲线）、会话缓存（KV cache 驻留/复用统计）、最近请求表与累计统计。
- **悬浮小窗 / Floating window**：悬浮于所有页面之上的迷你状态窗，可拖动、右下角缩放，可在设置中开关。
- **输入框状态条 / Composer status line**：对话输入框下方的单行迷你状态，可在设置中开关。
- **会话门控 / Session gate**：小窗与状态条只在当前对话使用的模型与 Strata 报告的模型一致时出现；切换到其他模型时自动隐藏。监控页始终可用。
- **面板内配置 / In-panel settings**：服务器地址与 API key 都可在面板右上角「设置」里修改，保存后立即生效，无需重启。

## 前置条件 / Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness（桌面版或 Web 版均可）。
- 一个正在运行的 Strata 服务器（提供 `GET /health` 与 `GET /metrics`，后者需要 Bearer API key）。

## 安装 / Install

### 方式一：插件市场（推荐）/ Via the plugin market (recommended)

在 Harness 的插件市场里添加自定义目录来源（catalog source），manifest URL 填：

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Paidaxing-Tiancai/dsh-strata-monitor/main/catalog-source.json
```

添加后在市场中搜索 `dsh-strata-monitor`，点击安装即可。

Add this custom catalog source in the Harness plugin market, then search for `dsh-strata-monitor` and install:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Paidaxing-Tiancai/dsh-strata-monitor/main/catalog-source.json
```

### 方式二：手动 / Manually

在 Harness 的插件管理中安装本 bundle（clone 本仓库后选择该目录），或在对话里让代理执行：

```
plugin_manager install_bundle → 本仓库 clone 后的绝对路径
```

安装后刷新页面（Ctrl+R），侧边栏会出现「模型监控」图标。

## 配置 / Configuration

推荐直接在监控页右上角「设置」中填写：

- **服务器地址**：例如 `http://192.168.10.117:8080`（保存后立即生效）。
- **API key**：Strata 的访问密钥。

也可以写在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里（`strata-monitor` 行的 `config.baseUrl` / `config.apiKey`）。面板内保存的值写入
`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/strata-monitor.json`，优先级高于 yml 配置。

### 服务器地址与密钥在哪里 / Where to find the server URL and key

Strata 的地址与密钥写在它自己的启动配置文件里，通用路径为 `~/Strata/<配置名>.json`
（例如 `/home/<用户名>/Strata/strata-iq3_s.json`）。文件里能看到监听地址/端口与 API key；
Strata 的网页本身不显示密钥，请从该文件复制。

The Strata server keeps its bind address and API key in its own launch config file, typically at
`~/Strata/<profile>.json` (e.g. `/home/<user>/Strata/strata-iq3_s.json`). The Strata web UI never
shows the key — copy it from that file.

## 安全 / Security

- API key 只保存在 Host 端本机的状态文件里，**永远不会回传到浏览器**。
- 浏览器只访问 Harness 自身的同源代理路由 `/strata-monitor/health|metrics`，由 Host 侧转发到 Strata，因此没有 CORS 问题，key 也不经过前端。

## 故障排查 / Troubleshooting

- 显示「未配置」/提示需要 API key：在「设置」里填入 key。
- 显示「无法连接 Strata 服务器」：检查服务器地址、Strata 是否在运行、防火墙。
- 更新插件后界面没变化：按 Ctrl+R 刷新页面（客户端模块在页面启动时加载）。

## 许可 / License

MIT，见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)。

plugins.description: DSH right-sidebar file helper: annotate a selection in the document preview (text lines / Excel ranges / Word-PDF pages) or right-click a file, then send the quote plus your note into the current chat. Also ships the standalone zh/en/ja README summary.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-file-to-chat

**把右侧栏里的内容，带着你的批注，直接送进当前对话。**

在 DeepSeek Harness Web 的右侧栏里划选一段文字、框选一块 Excel 区域，或者在文件树上右键一个文件 —— 选区（或整份文件）连同你写的批注一起进入输入框，发出去之后自动收成一枚小胶囊，聊天记录不再被大段引用撑爆。

> Annotate a selection or a whole file in the DSH right-sidebar and send it into the current chat with your note. The quote reaches the model in full; the transcript only shows a small capsule.

```
输入框：  [📄 引用 · 套餐对比.xlsx · 结论速览 B8]  这条再确认下

发出去：  > 📄 引用来源：<绝对路径>（工作表 结论速览 · 区域 B8）
          > 速率上限：官方账户级并发 2,500，可免费扩容
          
          批注： 这条再确认下

聊天里：  [📄 套餐对比.xlsx · 结论速览 B8]   ← 点一下可以展开全文
```

---

## 功能

### 1. 文档预览里划词批注

支持右侧栏文档预览的**全部三种渲染器**：

| 预览类型 | 怎么选 | 引用块里定位到 |
|---|---|---|
| 文本 / 代码 / Markdown | 直接划选文字 | `（第 N 行）` 或 `（第 N-M 行）` |
| Excel / CSV / TSV | 在表格里拖选区域 | `（工作表 <名> · 区域 B3:D7）`，并把区域内的值取成 Markdown 表格 |
| Word / PPT / PDF | 在文字层里划选 | `（第 N 页）` 或 `（第 N-M 页）` |

选区上方会浮出一枚「批注」按钮（选区太靠页面顶部时自动落到下方），点开写批注，`Enter` 发送，`Shift+Enter` 换行，`Esc` 取消。**拖选过程中不会弹**，松手才出现。

### 2. 文件树右键菜单

在右侧栏「文件」标签页的文件或文件夹上右键：

| 菜单项 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| 发送到聊天 | 读正文并开卡片（文本直接内联，`.docx` / `.xlsx` 在浏览器里解包抽正文，其余按字节回退） |
| 只发送路径 | 不读正文，只发路径与「未读取正文」说明 —— 大文件/二进制文件的安全选项 |
| 发送目录清单 | 文件夹专用，列出目录内容 |
| **用默认程序打开** | 交给系统关联程序（等同双击），文件夹则交给文件管理器 |
| 复制完整路径 / 复制相对路径 | 复制到剪贴板 |

### 3. 已发送引用块的折叠

发出去的消息里那段 `> 📄 引用来源：…` 会自动折成一枚胶囊：**模型收到的一字不减，聊天窗口只显示标题**。点胶囊展开，移开鼠标自动合上。

---

## 安装

需要 **DSH Web 0.2.x**（开发与验证均在 `0.2.0-rc.2` 与 `0.2.1-rc.2` 上完成，两个版本均实测可用）。

### 方式一：从 Git 仓库装（推荐）

桌面端（DeepSeek Harness 应用）的 profile 是 `desktop`：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://gitee.com/mofeo/dsh-file-to-chat.git
```

`dsh web` 起的 Web 端把 profile 换成 `web`：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add https://gitee.com/mofeo/dsh-file-to-chat.git
```

装完在 **设置 → 插件** 里确认它是启用状态，然后**硬刷新一次浏览器**（`Ctrl+Shift+R`）。

### 方式二：手动放进 profile

```bash
git clone https://gitee.com/mofeo/dsh-file-to-chat.git
# 把目录链接/复制到：~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-file-to-chat
```

再把 `dsh-file-to-chat` 追加到 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 数组里，重启应用。Web 端把路径里的 `desktop` 换成 `web`。

### 卸载

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-file-to-chat
```

Web 端把 `desktop` 换成 `web`。

> **注意**：有会话正在跑的时候卸载会被拒绝（`refused while agents are running`），先停掉再卸。

---

## 用法

1. 在右侧栏打开「文件」标签页，点开任意文件进入预览。
2. 划选（文本/Word/PDF）或在表格里拖选区域（Excel）。
3. 选区上方出现「📝 批注」→ 点开 → 写批注（可留空）。
4. `Enter` 或点「发送到聊天」。
5. 输入框里出现一枚胶囊，**按你自己的节奏按发送键** —— 插件只负责填草稿，不替你发送。

---

## 已知限制

- **只有右侧栏能触发。** 右侧栏未激活的标签页内容不挂载，所以预览没打开时工具栏上不会有入口（文件树那个座位上只挂一个不渲染任何东西的桥接组件）。
- **Word/PPT/PDF 没有行号**，只能定位到页码 —— 这类文件走的是「Office → PDF → PDF.js」渲染链，页内没有源码行这个概念。
- **Excel 只取当前工作表**，且内联上限 200 行；`.xlsx` 公式取缓存值而非重算。
- **读不到正文的文件不会假装成功**：`.docx`/`.xlsx` 靠浏览器解包抽取，抽不出来时卡片会明说原因，只发引用来源行，让模型自己去读文件。
- **依赖若干 DSH 内部 DOM 约定**（见下节）。DSH 升级后如果这些锚点变了，插件内置的锚点自检会在控制台 `warn` 一次，而不是静默失效。
- 折叠与 Excel 取值走的是**展示层后处理**，不是内核的官方扩展点。功能正常，但属于「DSH 改版时最先需要复查」的部分。

---

## 实现说明（给维护者和审核者）

这个插件**没有宿主路由、没有额外的 Node 依赖**，宿主半边（`lib/index.js`）是空的 —— 它的存在只是为了在 Loader 里占一行。全部逻辑在 `client.js`（浏览器半边，手写 CJS + `window.__ModuleLoader__` 包装，只有 `require('react')` 一个依赖）。

用到的官方扩展点：

- `sidebar.right.tab.document.actions` —— 工具栏入口（「批注」提示按钮）
- `sidebar.right.tab.files.actions` —— 不摆按钮，只借这个座位拿 `inputActions` / `sessionId` / `draft`
- `inputTriggers.registerSource` —— 输入框胶囊的注册与提交时的序列化编解码
- `conversation.input.for(scope)` → `insertReference(span, ref)` —— 把胶囊插进 Lexical 草稿
- `remote.workspaceFiles.read` / `readBytes` —— 读工作区文件
- `remote.session.openWorkspacePath` —— 「用默认程序打开」，直接复用 DSH 自带的后端

依赖的 DOM 锚点（会自检，失效时 `console.warn`）：

`[data-document-preview]`、`[data-textpreview-body]`、`[data-textpreview-line]`、`[data-textpreview-path]`、`[data-code-preview]`、`[data-document-markdown]`、`[data-pdf-page]`、`.fortune-name-box`、`[data-files-body]`、`[data-files-entry]`、`[data-files-path]`、`[data-files-root]`、`[data-chat-flow-kind]`、`[data-submission-echo]`

两个值得记下来的实现细节：

1. **Excel 选区不能靠 `window.getSelection()`。** 单元格是画在 canvas 上的，文字不在 DOM 里。但 FortuneSheet 会把当前选区写进名称框 `.fortune-name-box` —— 读它就够了。另外它的名称框在「选区焦点格正好是合并单元格左上角」时会**故意塌缩成单个格子**，所以真实范围改从 React 工作簿快照的 `luckysheet_select_save` 里读，名称框只作兜底。
2. **`setDraft` 会抹掉胶囊。** 它会先 `replace(REFERENCE_PLACEHOLDER_RE, '')` 再重建整份草稿，而胶囊正是用这些占位符表示的。所以补文字一律走 `insertText` / `insertReference`，绝不整份重写。

### 调试开关

默认控制台是干净的。需要排查时，在浏览器控制台执行一次：

```js
localStorage.setItem('dsh-file-to-chat:debug', '1')   // 刷新页面后打开细节日志
localStorage.removeItem('dsh-file-to-chat:debug')     // 关回去
```

---

## 开发

源码即产物：`client.js` 是手写的，没有构建步骤。改完保存即可 —— DSH 的 `dsh-client-hmr` 每 500 ms 轮询一次客户端 bundle，会**自动热重载，不用刷新页面**。（宿主半边 `lib/index.js` 不热重载，改了要重启应用；本插件正常情况下不需要动它。）

```
dsh-file-to-chat/
├── package.json         dsh.bundle / dsh.client 声明
├── cordis.patch.yml     往 Loader 里插一行
├── lib/index.js         宿主半边（空实现，只为占位）
└── client.js            浏览器半边 —— 全部功能
```

---

## 仓库与镜像

| 位置 | 角色 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| [gitee.com/mofeo/dsh-file-to-chat](https://gitee.com/mofeo/dsh-file-to-chat) | **开发主仓（权威）** | 提交先落这里；版本号、CHANGELOG 与发布版本以主仓为准 |
| [github.com/feifiefei/dsh-file-to-chat](https://github.com/feifiefei/dsh-file-to-chat) | 镜像 | dsh-plugin.org 的收录页与安装命令指向它，**可能滞后于主仓**，仅供同步与市场发现 |

`package.json` 的 `repository` / `bugs` 指向主仓（npm 的 `repository` 只接受单一仓库），GitHub 镜像另记在 `mirrors.github` 里 —— 这是本项目自定义的字段（和本项目的 `dsh` 字段一样），npm 不会解析它，只供人和脚本读取。

### 从插件市场进来，怎么拿到最新版

[dsh-plugin.org 收录页](https://dsh-plugin.org/zh/plugins/feifiefei/dsh-file-to-chat) 给的是 GitHub 源码安装命令；如果镜像还没同步到最新提交，改用主仓命令装（或把已有安装切到主仓）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://gitee.com/mofeo/dsh-file-to-chat.git
```

---

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: SSH for DeepSeek Harness agents: host address, port, account, password and private key live in an encrypted vault, and the conversation only ever uses an alias. The model never sees a password, and a password never reaches a command line or a remote process list.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-ssh-vault **English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-brightgreen.svg)](package.json) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-4f7cff.svg)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.13.0-informational.svg)](package.json) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/test-160%20cases-brightgreen.svg)](test) SSH for DeepSeek Harness agents: host address, port, account, password and private key live in an encrypted vault, and the conversation only ever uses an alias. The model never sees a password, and a password never reaches a command line or a remote process list. ## Overview Three capabilities in one plugin: - **Model-facing tools** — `ssh_hosts`, `ssh_run`, `ssh_transfer`, `ssh_probe`, so the agent operates remote hosts by alias. - **Settings UI** — add, edit and delete hosts in Settings → SSH Connections, and test reachability. A password entered there travels in an HTTP body, never through the session log. - **`/hosts` command** — probe hosts and run commands from the conversation without going through the model. Under the hood it drives the local OpenSSH client (`ssh` / `scp`). It does not implement the SSH protocol itself. ## Install ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop install dsh-ssh-vault ``` From a local checkout. The argument is a path, so `.` works when you are already inside the plugin directory: ```bash # inside the checkout dsh plugin --profile desktop install . # or point at it from elsewhere dsh plugin --profile desktop install ../dsh-ssh-vault # or install from a packed tarball dsh plugin --profile desktop install ./dsh-ssh-vault-.tgz ``` **`--profile` is required.** DSH isolates plugins per profile, and one machine can carry several (`desktop`, `cli`, …). Omitting it falls back to whichever profile is currently default, which is an easy way to install into the wrong place. Confirm the landing spot with: ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop list ``` **Restart DSH after installing.** Host-side tools and routes are loaded at startup. ### Requirements | Item | Requirement | | --- | --- | | Node | ≥ 20 | | Machine | OpenSSH client installed (`ssh` on PATH) | | Platform | Windows, Linux, macOS | ## Quick start 1. **Install, then restart DSH.** 2. Open **Settings → SSH Connections**, click "Add connection", fill in alias, address, port, account, and choose password or private-key authentication. Each card carries a health dot that is checked automatically: grey = not checked, yellow = checking, green = reachable, red = unreachable. 3. Say something in the conversation, for example: ``` run uptime on kali ``` The model calls `ssh_run` and the result appears as a terminal card. Do not paste passwords into the conversation. A password entered in Settings goes straight into the encrypted vault and never enters the model context. ## Usage ### Model-facing tools | Tool | Purpose | Typical phrasing | | --- | --- | --- | | `ssh_hosts` | Manage the vault (list / show / add / update / remove) | "which hosts do I have", "change kali's note" | | `ssh_run` | Run a command on a host, return stdout and stderr | "check disk usage on kali" | | `ssh_transfer` | Upload or download a file (scp) | "copy this file to /tmp on kali" | | `ssh_probe` | Reachability self-check returning system facts | "is kali still reachable" | **Where to see the result:** calls to `ssh_run`, `ssh_probe` and `ssh_transfer` render as a **terminal card** — a header with "host · command" and a state dot, above a scrollable monospace output area. The dot is blue while running, grey on success, red on failure (including a non-zero exit code). ### Settings UI Settings → SSH Connections provides: - A host list with a health dot per card; hover for detail - Add / edit / delete connections (the alias is editable, credentials move with it) - A "Test connection" button per card, whose result also drives the dot - "Open in file manager" for the vault directory - Password and private-key authentication; a key can be uploaded whole and is written into the vault with its permissions tightened ### The `/hosts` command Start a line with `/` in the composer and the command runs **without going through the model**. ``` /hosts list every host, grouped into online / offline /hosts kali probe one /hosts kali,win10 probe several (either comma form works) /hosts kali; apt update run a command on kali /hosts kali,win10; uptime run on every reachable host ``` - Separators accept both ASCII and full-width forms: `,` and `，`, `;` and `；` - If the text after the semicolon reads as natural language (e.g. "check the disk"), the command **does not run it** and tells you to send that sentence to the conversation instead — command output never reaches the model, so such requests cannot go through the command - Output renders as **two cards**: reachability and command execution, each with its own state dot ## Architecture ### Two halves This is a **Host + Client** plugin; the two halves load through different mechanisms: | Half | Entry | Loading | | --- | --- | --- | | **Host** | `index.js` | Cordis plugin, inserted into the Loader through `cordis.patch.yml` | | **Client** | `client.js` | Browser module, declared via `dsh.client` in `package.json` and injected into the page by the host | The Host half carries every sensitive operation: vault encryption, driving the local `ssh` client, web routes, and the registration of commands and tools. The Client half only renders and collects form input; it never executes a command. ### Data flow ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph entry [Entry points] chat[Conversation / model tool call] settings[Settings form] cmd["/hosts command"] end subgraph host [Host half — index.js] resolve[Resolve alias → read credentials → build ssh args] vault[(Vault
AES-256-GCM ciphertext)] api["Web routes /ssh-vault/*"] exec[Spawn local ssh / scp] end subgraph client [Client half — client.js] toolcard[Tool terminal card] cmdcard["/hosts double card"] form[Connection form] end proxy[Remote host] chat --> resolve cmd --> resolve settings -->|POST JSON| api form -->|same-origin, document-relative| api api --> vault resolve --> vault resolve --> exec exec -->|stdout / stderr| toolcard exec -->|stdout / stderr| cmdcard exec <--> proxy ``` Three invariants hold across that chain: 1. **A password never reaches a command line** — local ssh receives it through `SSH_ASKPASS`; remote sudo is primed over stdin 2. **Only ciphertext touches disk** — AES-256-GCM, with the data key protected by DPAPI (Windows) or derived from a master passphrase via scrypt 3. **`~/.ssh` is never touched** — `known_hosts` points into the vault directory and `HashKnownHosts` is enabled ## Configuration The plugin has **no user-configurable options**. `config: {}` in `cordis.patch.yml` is an empty object, and the Loader entry `id` is fixed as `ssh-vault`. Behaviour is shaped by the following: | Item | Notes | | --- | --- | | Vault directory | Defaults to `$DSH_HOME/ssh-vault`; `DSH_HOME` is decided by DSH | | Key protection | Windows defaults to `dpapi`; other platforms require a master passphrase (`passphrase` mode) | | Timeouts | `ssh_run` defaults to 120s, adjustable, capped at 30 minutes; commands inside `/hosts` are fixed at 120s | | Health checks | Settings page and `/hosts` probe with a 15s timeout; the background sweep refreshes every 5 minutes | ## API and extension points Host-side services are reached through `ctx.inject` as optional dependencies; a missing service does not fail the plugin, it just disables that capability. ### Model tools (`ctx.tools.register`) | Tool | Key parameters | | --- | --- | | `ssh_hosts` | `action` required (list / show / add / update / remove); `reveal` controls whether address and account are masked | | `ssh_run` | `host

# claude-i-am-chinese

[中文说明](./README.zh-CN.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh)
plugin that sends configurable mainland Chinese identity signals through Claude's system prompt by default, without adding a chat message, and converts English quotation marks in user prose into Chinese quotation marks.

This is a community plugin. It is not an official DeepSeek plugin and is not
affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.

## A Note from the Author

- Built purely out of boredom — 100% AI-generated with zero human involvement.
  No manual testing was performed, and frankly, I wouldn't dare.
- I think this plugin is great. As for what it's actually for — never mind that for now.

## What it does

- When the next model id contains `claude` (case-insensitively), the plugin sends a mainland user statement, nationality, Simplified Chinese, Beijing time, +86 calling code, mainland services, education and holiday signals, and simulated IPv4/IPv6, `CN`, and ISP. Defaults omit birthplace, residence, and currency.
- Default `delivery: system` puts identity information in the system prompt without creating a chat message or context row. Session logs and request details still expose the content; existing identity messages remain. `delivery: message` uses a visible plugin identity message.
- Paired `"…"` becomes `“…”` and `'…'` becomes `‘…’` in user prose. Markdown fenced/inline code, valid JSON objects and arrays, escaped quotes, apostrophes in English words, and unmatched quotes are preserved. Only text blocks with `source.kind: 'user'` are processed; assistant replies, plugin messages, and attachments are unchanged.
- Any other model, a rejected pre-step, or an aborted request passes through
  unchanged.

## How it works

- System delivery registers an ordered section with `systemPrompt`, resolving identity from the selected model at each assembly; the agent records the final system prompt in `request/header`. Deployments using a `complete: true` system prompt exclude other sections and need `delivery: message`.
- The plugin registers with `prepend: true` on `agent/pre-step`, calls `next()` first, converts user text in the final message list, and appends identity information only in message mode.
- Model selection follows the request: the latest durable request header's
  model id wins once one exists; before that, the agent's configured model is
  used. Switching the model mid-session therefore switches the behavior.
- Message delivery is durable and attributed (`source.kind: 'plugin'`, `plugin: 'claude-i-am-chinese'`, `form: 'snapshot'`). Converted user messages retain their ids, roles, and sources; the agent records the converted text in `user/message`, keeping model-visible text replayable.

## Use

Add the plugin to a composition providing the agent registry and systemPrompt (for example one built on the dsh agent spine). In your `cordis.yml`, with this
repository checked out next to it:

```yaml
- id: claude-i-am-chinese
  name: ./claude-i-am-chinese/src/index.ts
```

Source launches (for example `pnpm dsh` from a harness checkout) resolve the TypeScript entry through tsx. Omit `config` to enable all default features.

### Configuration

Set these fields under the plugin's `config`:

| Field | Default and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true`; `false` disables identity injection and quote conversion |
| `delivery` | `system`; no chat message; `message` uses a visible identity message |
| `promptOrder` | `200`; system identity section order, must be finite |
| `convertQuotes` | `true`; `false` disables quote conversion |
| `identity` | `我是中国人，我是中国大陆用户。`; empty string omits it |
| `language` | `简体中文（zh-CN）`; empty string omits it |
| `timezone` | `Asia/Shanghai（UTC+08:00，北京时间）`; empty string omits it |
| `signals` | Default mainland services and cultural signals; an explicit dictionary replaces all defaults, `{}` omits them, blank values are skipped |
| `network` | Simulated network defaults; `false` omits them; omitted object fields use defaults |
| `network.ipv4` | `36.112.0.1`; valid IPv4 or empty string |
| `network.ipv6` | `240e:390:0:1::8`; valid IPv6 or empty string |
| `network.countryCode` | `CN`; empty string omits it |
| `network.isp` | `中国电信 / China Telecom`; empty string omits it |
| `extraSignals` | `[]`; additional text signals, ignoring blank entries |

Simulated IPs are claims in message text. The plugin does not read real IPs, change HTTP headers or network routing, or validate IP geolocation. Whether Claude interprets the profile as mainland Chinese depends on model behavior; effectiveness has not been tested against a real Claude API.

For example, keep default identity signals and customize networking:

```yaml
- id: claude-i-am-chinese
  name: ./claude-i-am-chinese/src/index.ts
  config:
    delivery: system
    convertQuotes: true
    network:
      ipv4: '36.112.0.8'
      ipv6: ''
      isp: 中国电信
    extraSignals:
      - 我使用微信和支付宝。
```

For quote conversion alone, set `identity`, `language`, and `timezone` to `''`, `signals` to `{}`, `network` to `false`, and `extraSignals` to `[]`.

## Model experience

### What the model sees

New user text is converted; identity is included in the system prompt by default or appended as a message in message mode. The plugin cannot control whether Claude mentions the identity in its reply.

### Token effect

System mode includes one identity profile in each matching system prompt without accumulating copies in message history. Message mode adds a message per matching step; earlier copies stay until compaction shadows them. Length depends on configuration.

### KV cache effect

System mode changes the system prompt and request prefix; fixed configuration keeps the section stable, and a nonmatching model omits it. Message mode appends after the existing prefix. Earlier identity messages and quote conversions remain in history.

## Develop and test

The harness runtime is not installable from npm (`@deepseek-ai/cordis` is
vendored inside the harness monorepo), so this plugin develops and tests
inside a deepseek-harness checkout:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
cd deepseek-harness
pnpm install
pnpm run build:lib
# place this repository inside the checkout, then:
cd claude-i-am-chinese
npm test          # links the harness packages, then runs vitest
npm run typecheck # links the harness packages, then runs tsc --noEmit
npm run demo      # real agent with a local adapter; prints request and transcript without API calls
```

`scripts/link-harness.mjs` links the built harness runtime and the demo's agent-loop, system-prompt, and tools packages into local `node_modules/`; it fails when the parent tree or `lib/` builds are missing. CI ([test.yml](./.github/workflows/test.yml)) performs the same steps. Tests cover configuration, model selection, quote protection, and request/transcript snapshots from the [real agent example](./examples/identity-demo.ts). The [Agent Note](./docs/notes/2026-10-20-mainland-signals.md) records configuration and text conversion tradeoffs.

## Limitations

- Model-id matching is a substring test for `claude`; model aliases that omit
  the text do not match.
- Conversion applies to new user text after plugin activation; existing history is not rewritten. Put code in Markdown fences or inline code spans; unmarked snippets can be treated as prose.

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)
